score_rationale: The paper contains a potentially important and formally verified law-level stability theory, but substantial claim-scope, computational, reproducibility, positioning, and organizational problems prevent the current manuscript from earning publication.
summary: The paper establishes a Lipschitz map from observable proxy summaries to the quotient law of latent-class mean treatment effects under fixed latent cardinality, bounded contributions, latent-arm positivity, and uniform proxy-rank margins. It develops root-n estimators, honest Wasserstein confidence sets, cluster reports, and separated-stratum ordered-weight rates, with matching lower bounds on an explicit two-class specialization. The formal results are strong and appear faithfully represented at the theorem level, but the reader-facing manuscript needs major revision to distinguish the estimand from an individual-effect distribution, delimit its exact-real computational claims, expose the required validity types and known conditioning inputs, document verification reproducibly, and position the rates against the closest literature.
strengths: The gap-free Lipschitz modulus is a clean and potentially significant contribution: it treats collisions through the quotient probability law while preserving explicit fixed-margin conditions.
The upper theory is unusually comprehensive, connecting population stability to measurable estimators, finite-sample tail bounds, honest Wasserstein confidence sets, and component-level reporting.

The explicit two-class witnesses place the local lower bounds inside the proxy-causal model with strict positivity and full proxy rank, rather than importing a lower bound from an unrelated mixture experiment.
The manuscript generally qualifies the matching minimax results as applying to the displayed two-class specialization and carries theorem-local scope footnotes for its VMW publication-level inputs.
The dedicated related-work section and sentence-case headings comply with the requested high-level organization and typography.

findings.issue: The sentence "This target is a causal distribution of treatment-effect values" can be read as identifying the distribution of unit-level effects, whereas each atom is the latent-class mean contrast \(E[Y(1)\mid U=u]-E[Y(0)\mid U=u]\). Similar phrases such as "distribution of latent treatment effects" recur in the abstract and discussion without consistently preserving that distinction.
findings.fix: Describe \(\nu_P\) throughout as the population-weighted distribution of latent-class average treatment effects, and explicitly distinguish it at first use from the distribution of individual contrasts \(Y(1)-Y(0)\). Consider revising the title and abstract to include "latent-class mean effects" if the shorter terminology would otherwise remain ambiguous.

findings.section: Confidence sets, cluster reports, and ordered weights
findings.issue: The abstract calls the confidence set and report "computable," while \cref{obj:def:cluster-report} says the report is "computed from \(\widehat S_n\), \(S(P)\), ..." and includes \(K_C(P)\) and \(\Delta_C(P)\). The latter are oracle objects used to state validity, not observable inputs. Moreover, the verified computational guarantee is an explicit finite constrained representation in a fixed-dimensional unit-cost exact-real model, rather than a conventional bit-complexity or implemented numerical guarantee.
findings.fix: Split the section into a data-only reporting algorithm, using only \(\widehat\lambda_n\), fixed class constants, and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\), followed by separate true-law notation used solely in the validity theorem. Qualify every "computable" or "sample-evaluable" claim with the exact-real model and distinguish finite constrained representability, exact evaluation, polynomial operation count for the lattice search, and unresolved polynomial-time computation of the sharp repaired-image set.

findings.issue: The displayed "Atomic law coordinates" definition denotes \(\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) by unrestricted real weight and location coordinates, while subsequent definitions and theorems use the same notation for probability laws. The manuscript never clearly separates the raw coordinate record, the valid subtype with nonnegative unit-sum masses and bounded locations, and the quotient by equality of induced measures. This leaves the domains of \(W_1\), the atom-floor condition, estimators, and confidence sets unclear to the reader.
findings.fix: Introduce three explicit types in order: raw labelled coordinates, valid represented probability laws, and quotient laws. State all validity conditions and explain which notation is used by each estimator and confidence set. Reserve \(\mathcal P_{\le k}\) for the valid probability-law class, or rename the unrestricted record so it cannot be mistaken for that class.

findings.issue: The exposition is not organized in dependency order. Thresholded inverses, transport plans, confidence radii, endpoint feasibility, candidate counts, and structured operators appear before the observed record, model class, empirical summary, and quotient law are fully defined. Exact or near-exact duplicates include the empirical summary, KL divergence, summary radius, thresholded pseudoinverse, matrix action/operator norm, and several lattice objects.
findings.fix: Rebuild the setup in the order observed/full-data records, causal and proxy assumptions, population moments, model class, quotient-law type, empirical summary, and derived spectral objects. Move estimator-specific definitions to the estimation section and confidence-specific objects to the confidence section. Delete duplicate environments and add a one-page notation-and-results roadmap or dependency diagram.

findings.issue: The section cites the relevant literatures but rarely compares actual results. In particular, it does not state the separated-parameter rate and conditions of the closest VMW theorem, the collision-dependent rates from ordinary finite-mixture theory, or why the present proxy-summary geometry permits root-n quotient-law estimation where standard overfitted-mixture settings exhibit slower Wasserstein rates.
findings.fix: Add a precise comparison table or several focused paragraphs reporting the targets, assumptions, and rates of VMW Theorem 7.2 and the closest mixture results, including the local rate from Heinrich--Kahn and the relevant Wasserstein rates from Wu--Yang and Doss--Wu--Yang--Zhou. Explain which structural feature of the observable proxy operator changes the local geometry, and verify every numerical rate and theorem locator against the cited source.

findings.issue: The author footnote asserts that "the verification appendix records the exact scope, toolchain, and commit," but the displayed appendix supplies no Lean version, dependency version, repository or archive location, build command, or commit identifier. The generic statement that proofs are machine-checked is therefore not independently reproducible from the submission.
findings.fix: Add an artifact subsection giving the exact commit corresponding to the verified declarations, the Lean and dependency versions, repository or archival URL, clean-build commands, expected outputs, and a table mapping each manuscript object to its declaration. Ensure the manuscript and archived source are generated from the same identified revision.

findings.issue: The procedures depend on \(k,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), including the threshold \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\), lattice geometry, atom floor, and confidence radius, but the manuscript alternates between calling these constants fixed and calling the estimator sample-evaluable without clearly saying which bounds must be supplied to the procedure. The economic content, plausibility, and sensitivity of joint latent-arm positivity and feature-matrix singular-value margins also receive little discussion.
findings.fix: State prominently that the theory uses known class dimensions and supplied uniform envelope, positivity, and rank bounds. Explain how each bound enters estimation and reporting, whether conservative bounds remain valid, and how misspecification affects the claimed guarantees. Place unknown-cardinality or unknown-margin adaptation in the explicitly titled Open questions or Limitations material.

findings.issue: The opening sentence, "The law-level and ordered-weight upper bounds have matching converse statements on explicit local experiments," initially sounds like a converse for the full arbitrary-\(k\) upper-bound classes. The verified matching minimax results are established on the displayed \(k=d_x=d_z=2\) specialization, while the VMW transfer carries only the witness-pair lower bounds.
findings.fix: Begin the section by stating that rate matching is proved on the explicit uniformly conditioned two-class specialization. Repeat that qualifier whenever "matching," "sharp," or "same-class" is used, and state affirmatively that the VMW transfer delivers witness-containment lower bounds for comparator classes.

findings.issue: The phrase "a sharp summary-inversion set" suggests an optimality or minimality result that is not stated. The theorem establishes coverage and a diameter bound for the exact repaired-image construction.
findings.fix: Replace "sharp summary-inversion set" with "exact repaired-image summary-inversion set" unless the authors add and prove a formal sharpness criterion.

findings.issue: Reader-facing references such as "the \leanref{P-4}{compressed observable operator}" and symbol links through \leanref do not follow the manuscript's exclusive cleveref cross-reference contract and expose opaque internal identifiers.
findings.fix: Replace every reader-facing \leanref target with ordinary prose for symbols or with \cref/\Cref pointing to the exact anchored definition or result. Remove internal identifiers such as "P-4" from the reader-facing manuscript.

findings.issue: The sentence "Published inputs used as cited mathematical facts enter through theorem-local citation boundaries" is too vague, and the earlier introduction additionally mentions "standard probability or selection primitives" at such boundaries. The current dependency record identifies publication-level VMW scope inputs for the two starred results; it does not identify a separate external selection or probability dependency.
findings.fix: Enumerate the exact externally supplied VMW claims and the two manuscript results that use them. State separately that the remaining verified declarations have no recorded external publication dependency beyond their displayed hypotheses, and remove the stale suggestion of additional probability or selection trust boundaries.

findings.section: Confidence sets, cluster reports, and ordered weights
findings.issue: The paper presents the structured lattice and cluster report as operative computational contributions but provides no numerical example showing candidate growth, runtime, clustering behavior, coverage, or mass-interval width near a collision. The exact-real complexity exponent can be large even at fixed dimensions, so formal polynomial growth alone gives little guidance about practical use.
findings.fix: Add a reproducible two-class simulation using the displayed witness family, reporting runtime and coverage across homogeneous, near-collision, and separated regimes. Show the empirical components, support intervals, and mass intervals as the gap changes, and clearly label the implementation's numerical approximations relative to the exact-real theorem.

questions_for_authors: Is the intended applied estimand exclusively the distribution of latent-class average treatment effects, or do the authors intend any interpretation involving the distribution of individual treatment effects?
Which of \(k,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\) are assumed known to the analyst, and what guarantee is intended when conservative or misspecified values are supplied?
Does "computable" mean exact-real finite constrained representability, an implemented numerical algorithm, or polynomial bit complexity?
Where can a referee obtain the exact Lean artifact, dependency lockfile, build instructions, and revision corresponding to the submission?
